Section B: Education

text: Matriarchy is not typical in many families or societies. Family functions and family roles are diverse
and changing. These functions and roles are different depending on an individual’s gender, ethnicity
or social class. Sociologists debate whether these changes are positive or negative for society.

Section C: Crime, deviance and social control

text: Some sociologists argue that the education system can lead to social mobility. There are many
factors that influence educational achievement, for example home factors and teachers. Some
sociologists argue that schools can disadvantage female students. There are many different types
of schools, such as private schools.

Section D: Media

text: Sociologists use different measurements of crime. These measurements show that males commit
more crime than females. There are many deterrents to crime. Sociologists debate whether formal
or informal social control is more effective at preventing crime.

text: Many sociologists believe in the hypodermic-syringe model. Both traditional and new media can
have a negative impact on children. Sociologists agree that advertising plays an important role in
the media. However, sociologists debate whether the pluralist view of the media is the most accurate.
